newsitem.title: USA: INBRAND drops as growth falls below expectations.
newsitem.headline: INBRAND drops as growth falls below expectations.

text.p: INBRAND Corp's share price fell sharply Thursday after the company said it did not expect to see positive effects of its international consolidation efforts until fiscal 1998.

INBRAND, in a statement accompanying its fiscal second quarter earnings report yesterday, also said its gains in net sales and income for the quarter, and for the first half, were below its expectations.
INBRAND was down 7-1/2 to 12-1/2 at midday.

Atlanta-based INBRAND posted second quarter earnings of $2.1 million, or $0.18 a share, on net sales of $57.9 million, compared to earnings of $1.3 million, or $0.11 a share, on sales of $27.0 million a year earlier.

"Our international operations are... aiding our overall corporate gains, but we have not yet accomplished all our goals in consolidating the acquired businesses into a cohesive organization," said INBRAND Chairman Garnett Smith.
"We have recently made some key personnel changes which we believe will enable us to realize a higher return on the resources we now control in England and France.
"We expect some impact from these changes over the balance of fiscal 1997 but believe that the more meaningful strides will be made in fiscal 1998," Smith said.
Merrill Lynch said it cut its near-term rating on INBRAND to neutral from accumulate but kept its long-term rating at buy.
Robinson-Humphrey cut its near- and long-term ratings on INBRAND to market perform from buy.
INBRAND makes disposable adult incontinence and feminine hygiene products.
